rows.selection_reason: No prior evidence exists, so the first experiment should establish the simplest, most interpretable baseline to anchor all subsequent comparisons. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the minimal RNA configuration with a standard, well-understood encoder (PCA to 2000 dims) and no aggregation or fusion complexity. This tests whether a basic single-modality RNA model provides a meaningful accuracy floor. Establishing this baseline first is critical because: (1) it tells us whether RNA signal alone is sufficient or whether we must invest remaining budget in image/multimodal directions; (2) it provides a reference accuracy against which every more complex configuration (multiprofile, learned encoders, multimodal fusion) can be judged for marginal benefit; (3) it changes the fewest design choices, so any future performance difference can be attributed to a specific axis rather than confounded by multiple simultaneous changes. With 9 experiments remaining, this single clean baseline maximizes the information gained per experiment and guides the next logical step (e.g., adding image modality or upgrading the encoder).

The only completed experiment (config_001: RNA-only, PCA, single profile) yielded a weak 48.5% accuracy, giving us a single low baseline with no information about whether the image modality carries useful signal. The most critical uncertainty right now is whether image features contribute at all, since the entire premise of 'multimodal cellular profiling' depends on it. Config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) is the cleanest way to isolate the image modality's contribution: it matches config_001's singleprofile setting and uses a standard pretrained encoder (resnet50) analogous to PCA as a 'default' representation, so the comparison directly tests modality value without confounding fusion strategy, aggregation, or encoder complexity. If image-only accuracy substantially exceeds 48.5%, it justifies investing remaining budget in multimodal fusion; if it is comparable or worse, we should focus on improving RNA representations (scvi, scgpt) and profile settings. This single experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about the most important design axis with 8 experiments still remaining.

Evidence: RNA-only with PCA (config_001) achieves 48.5% accuracy while image-only with ResNet50 (config_010) is far weaker at 20.8%, establishing RNA as the dominant modality. The only RNA encoder tested so far is a linear PCA projection, which is a relatively simple baseline. Uncertainty: We do not yet know whether a learned nonlinear RNA encoder (scgpt, a pretrained single-cell foundation model) can substantially improve the RNA representation and thus validation accuracy. This experiment (config_007: rna_only, singleprofile, scgpt) isolates the effect of the RNA encoder by changing only that one variable relative to config_001. It is the best next step because (1) it directly targets the most impactful design axis (RNA representation quality) given RNA's clear dominance, (2) scgpt is the most advanced encoder available and most likely to yield a large gain if any encoder upgrade will help, and (3) the result will inform whether to invest remaining budget in multimodal fusion with a strong RNA backbone or to focus on other axes like multiprofile aggregation.

Evidence: config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the best result so far at 0.485 accuracy, clearly outperforming image_only/resnet50 (0.208) and rna_only/scgpt (0.411). This establishes PCA-2000 RNA as the strongest single-modality baseline. Uncertainty: We have not yet tested whether multiprofile aggregation can improve upon the single-profile result. This experiment tests config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool), which is a minimal, single-variable extension of the best result—changing only the profile setting from single to multi and adding a simple average-pool aggregation. This isolates the effect of multiprofile on the top RNA encoder. It is the best use of experiment 4 because: (1) it directly extends the strongest configuration, (2) it uses the simplest aggregation (avgpool) before testing more complex ones, (3) the outcome will determine whether to invest remaining budget in multiprofile variants (transformer aggregation, multimodal multiprofile) or pivot to other directions (scvi_n200, better image encoders, multimodal fusion).

The best result so far is config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) at 0.5907 accuracy, a large jump over singleprofile PCA (0.4849). The most direct and informative next step is to test whether transformer aggregation outperforms avgpool for the same multiprofile PCA setup (config_003). This isolates a single variable (aggregation method) while holding the best-performing encoder and profile setting constant. Clarifying the optimal aggregation strategy before moving to multimodal fusion is critical: it determines whether we should pair transformer or avgpool with image fusion in the remaining 5 experiments, and avoids wasting budget on a suboptimal aggregation in more complex multimodal configs.

The best result so far is config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) at 0.5907 accuracy. Image alone (resnet50) is very weak (0.2079), raising the question of whether adding it in fusion provides any complementary signal. Config_018 extends the proven best RNA configuration by adding resnet50 image features with concat fusion while keeping the same multiprofile + avgpool setup, isolating the effect of multimodal fusion. This is the highest-value experiment because: (1) it directly tests whether the weak image modality adds information beyond strong RNA, (2) if it helps, the remaining 4 experiments can optimize fusion strategy (weighted), image encoder (ViT-L), or RNA encoder; if it doesn't, we can redirect budget to RNA-only improvements like scvi_n200 with multiprofile. Testing the simplest fusion (concat) with the best-known RNA setup first avoids confounding multiple changes.

The current best is config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) at 0.619 acc. The most direct and informative next step is to isolate the effect of fusion strategy by switching only concat→weighted (config_019), keeping all other settings identical. This is a clean single-variable comparison that tells us whether weighted fusion can further improve on the best result. Evidence so far shows image adds ~2.8% over RNA multiprofile alone, so the fusion mechanism is a plausible lever. With 3 experiments remaining after this, confirming or ruling out the fusion effect here keeps the remaining budget free to test other high-impact dimensions (e.g., ViT-L image encoder or scvi_n200 RNA encoder) from a known-best baseline.

The current best (config_019, 0.639 acc) uses multimodal + multiprofile + pca_n2000 + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted. All design axes except the image encoder have been validated: avgpool > transformer, weighted > concat, multiprofile > single, and multimodal > RNA-only. The image encoder is the only unexplored dimension in the best configuration. Image-only resnet50 scored only 0.208, suggesting the image signal may be underutilized; a larger ViT-L encoder (imagenet_vit_l) could extract richer spatial features that complement the RNA modality. Config_025 changes only the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l while keeping all other validated settings identical, isolating the encoder effect. This is the highest-information single-variable test: if it improves, we confirm a better image encoder is the key lever; if not, we confirm resnet50 is sufficient and can focus remaining budget on other axes. With 2 experiments left, this cleanly partitions the remaining search space.

The current best is config_019 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) at 0.6390. All other settings in this configuration are well-supported: multiprofile+avgpool beats singleprofile and transformer aggregation (0.591 vs 0.519 in RNA-only), weighted fusion beats concat (0.639 vs 0.619), and resnet50 marginally edges imagenet_vit_l (0.639 vs 0.635). The one untested dimension is the RNA encoder: scvi_n200 has not been evaluated in any experiment. Config_031 changes only the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 while holding all other parameters at their proven-optimal settings, making it a clean single-variable comparison. This tests whether a learned nonlinear latent representation (scvi) captures complementary information beyond PCA's linear projection, which could push accuracy above 0.639. With only one experiment remaining after this, a clean test of the last unexplored variable on the best-known backbone is the highest-value use of the slot: if it improves, we gain a new best; if not, we confirm pca_n2000 is optimal and finalize with confidence in config_019.

The current best is config_031 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) at 0.678 acc. The key evidence: scvi_n200 substantially outperformed pca_n2000 as RNA encoder (0.678 vs 0.639), suggesting a richer RNA latent space shifts the information balance in fusion. With pca_n2000, resnet50 and imagenet_vit_l were nearly tied (0.639 vs 0.635), but that comparison was made with a simpler RNA representation. This experiment (config_037) isolates the image encoder variable by swapping resnet50 → imagenet_vit_l while keeping scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool, and weighted fusion fixed. The hypothesis is that a stronger image encoder (ViT-L) can better match the information richness of scvi_n200 and provide complementary morphological features that ResNet50 misses. As the final experiment, this is the highest-probability single-variable exploitation to push past 0.678, since all other untested changes (transformer aggregation, concat fusion) have prior evidence of underperforming their alternatives.
